design.concept: A working ledger for the finance team: the queue of approved expenses is the main surface (dense table, category filter above it, applied filters as removable tokens), and a fixed side panel next to it shows the chosen expense and the payment-date form. The person scans the queue, clicks a row, checks the data and registers the payment without leaving the table or losing the filter.
design.decisions: One view, so no scene host: the table and the panel are always side by side on desktop. I did not use the side-detail-table's own Detail panel because registering the payment removes the expense from the queue, and the row's Detail would vanish together with the confirmation. A separate panel stays and shows the paid expense with its payment date as the success feedback, in place and without a page banner. Table: ml-data-table, amount last, right-aligned in tabular figures, status chip with text, selected row marked by index. Filter: one search bar for the category (the only text filter the contract takes). The collaborator filter is an entry parameter, so it is never typed and only appears as a removable token when active. Totals and counts are left out because the contract delivers none and the page must not compute them. Pagination is a 'load more' that appends, driven by hasMore, since the contract has no total of pages. Errors of the queue appear above the rows with a retry. The payment form shows only while the loaded expense is approved. The button is disabled until a date exists and shows loading while the command runs. The pagination-control and toast molecules were skipped: no page count exists, and the confirmation stays inline in the panel.
